text: Three website myths that quietly cost you customers.
Myth one: everything has to fit above the fold.
The fold is the bottom of the first screen, before anyone scrolls.
But people do scroll. A 2018 eye-tracking study found over 40% of viewing time was below the fold.
say: But people do scroll. A twenty eighteen eye tracking study found over forty percent of viewing time was below the fold.

text: So the top just needs to say what you do, where, and one clear next step.
Myth two: my work comes from word of mouth, so I don't need a website.
But when a mate recommends a tradie, what do you do before calling? You look them up.
If nothing comes up, or the site looks abandoned, that referral can go cold.
Myth three: once the website is built, it's done.
A website is more like a ute. It needs servicing. Software updates, current prices, new photos of your work.
Skip that, and things break quietly. Customers see old prices, and the footer still says 2019.
